title: Lifts along a quasi-isomorphism into a bounded below complex of injectives are unique up to homotopy
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $K^\bullet$, $L^\bullet$, $I^\bullet$ be cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $I^\bullet$ is bounded below ($I^n=0$ for $n\ll0$) and every $I^n$ is an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $\alpha:K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism and $\beta_1,\beta_2:L^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ morphisms of complexes such that $\beta_1\circ\alpha$ and $\beta_2\circ\alpha$ are chain-homotopic (for instance equal). Then $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are chain-homotopic: there are morphisms $k^n:L^n\to I^{n-1}$ with $\beta_1^n-\beta_2^n=d_I^{n-1}k^n+k^{n+1}d_L^n$ for all $n$.

proof.text: *Mapping cylinder.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-mapping-cylinder-split-factorization] to $\alpha:K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ (an abelian category is additive): there are a complex $\tilde L^\bullet$ and morphisms of complexes $\tilde\alpha:K^\bullet\to\tilde L^\bullet$, $\pi:\tilde L^\bullet\to L^\bullet$, $s:L^\bullet\to\tilde L^\bullet$ with $\pi\tilde\alpha=\alpha$, $\pi s=\mathrm{id}_{L^\bullet}$, $s\pi$ homotopic to $\mathrm{id}_{\tilde L^\bullet}$, and $\tilde\alpha$ a termwise split injection: $\tilde L^n\cong K^n\oplus M^n$ with $\tilde\alpha^n$ the inclusion of $K^n$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy, line 6481), direct argument of the proof (lines 6498-6537)

proof.text: *$\tilde\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism.* By [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology] (b), homotopic morphisms induce the same map on $H^n$, so $H^n(s)H^n(\pi)=H^n(s\pi)=\mathrm{id}$, and $H^n(\pi)H^n(s)=H^n(\pi s)=\mathrm{id}$ by functoriality of $H^n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence $H^n(\pi)$ is an isomorphism and $H^n(\tilde\alpha)=H^n(\pi)^{-1}H^n(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$, i.e. $\tilde\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy, line 6481), direct argument of the proof (lines 6498-6537)

proof.text: *Reduction to $\alpha$ termwise split.* Put $\beta_i'=\beta_i\pi:\tilde L^\bullet\to I^\bullet$. Then $\beta_i'\tilde\alpha=\beta_i\alpha$, so $\beta_1'\tilde\alpha$ and $\beta_2'\tilde\alpha$ are homotopic. Suppose $\beta_1'-\beta_2'=dk+kd$ for morphisms $k^n:\tilde L^n\to I^{n-1}$. Since $\pi s=\mathrm{id}$ we get $\beta_1-\beta_2=(\beta_1'-\beta_2')s=d(ks)+(ks)d$, using $s^{n+1}d_L^n=d_{\tilde L}^ns^n$; so $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are homotopic by the maps $k^ns^n$. Therefore, replacing $(L^\bullet,\alpha,\beta_1,\beta_2)$ by $(\tilde L^\bullet,\tilde\alpha,\beta_1',\beta_2')$ (step 2 keeps $\alpha$ a quasi-isomorphism), we may assume that $L^n=K^n\oplus M^n$ with $\alpha^n$ the inclusion of the first summand for every $n$: there are morphisms $p^n:L^n\to K^n$, $q^n:L^n\to M^n$, $j^n:M^n\to L^n$ with $p^n\alpha^n=\mathrm{id}$, $q^nj^n=\mathrm{id}$, $q^n\alpha^n=0$, $p^nj^n=0$, $\alpha^np^n+j^nq^n=\mathrm{id}_{L^n}$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy, line 6481), direct argument of the proof (lines 6498-6537)

proof.text: *The quotient complex.* Put $d_M^n=q^{n+1}d_L^nj^n:M^n\to M^{n+1}$. Then $q^{n+1}d_L^n=q^{n+1}d_L^n(\alpha^np^n+j^nq^n)=q^{n+1}\alpha^{n+1}d_K^np^n+d_M^nq^n=d_M^nq^n$, so $q$ commutes with the differentials, and $d_M^{n+1}d_M^n=q^{n+2}d_L^{n+1}(\mathrm{id}-\alpha^{n+1}p^{n+1})d_L^nj^n=-q^{n+2}\alpha^{n+2}d_K^{n+1}p^{n+1}d_L^nj^n=0$. So $M^\bullet$ is a complex, $q:L^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ is a morphism of complexes, and $0\to K^\bullet\xrightarrow{\alpha}L^\bullet\xrightarrow{q}M^\bullet\to0$ is short exact in each degree (it is split in each degree). Moreover, if $\psi:L^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ is a morphism of complexes with $\psi\alpha=0$, then $\psi=\psi(\alpha p+jq)=\varphi q$ with $\varphi^n=\psi^nj^n$, and $\varphi$ is a morphism of complexes: $\varphi^{n+1}d_M^n=\psi^{n+1}j^{n+1}q^{n+1}d_L^nj^n=\psi^{n+1}d_L^nj^n=d_I^n\psi^nj^n=d_I^n\varphi^n$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy, line 6481), direct argument of the proof (lines 6498-6537)

proof.text: *$M^\bullet$ is acyclic.* By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] the short exact sequence of step 4 gives an exact sequence $H^n(K)\xrightarrow{H^n(\alpha)}H^n(L)\xrightarrow{H^n(q)}H^n(M)\xrightarrow{\delta^n}H^{n+1}(K)\xrightarrow{H^{n+1}(\alpha)}H^{n+1}(L)$. Since $H^n(\alpha)$ is surjective, $H^n(q)=0$ (its kernel is the image of $H^n(\alpha)$), so $\delta^n$ is a monomorphism (its kernel is the image of $H^n(q)$); since $H^{n+1}(\alpha)$ is a monomorphism, the image of $\delta^n$, which is the kernel of $H^{n+1}(\alpha)$, is $0$, so $\delta^n=0$. Hence $H^n(M)=0$ for all $n$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy, line 6481), direct argument of the proof (lines 6498-6537)

proof.text: *Correcting $\beta_1-\beta_2$ on $K^\bullet$.* By hypothesis there are $h^n:K^n\to I^{n-1}$ with $\beta_1^n\alpha^n-\beta_2^n\alpha^n=d_I^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d_K^n$. Put $\bar h^n=h^np^n:L^n\to I^{n-1}$ (equal to $h^n$ on $K^n$ and zero on $M^n$; Stacks writes $h=h_1-h_2$ from the two homotopies to $\gamma$, here $\gamma=\beta_1\alpha$) and $\psi=\beta_1-\beta_2-(d_I\bar h+\bar hd_L)$. A map of the form $d\bar h+\bar hd$ commutes with the differentials, so $\psi$ is a morphism of complexes, and $\psi^n\alpha^n=\beta_1^n\alpha^n-\beta_2^n\alpha^n-d_I^{n-1}h^np^n\alpha^n-h^{n+1}p^{n+1}\alpha^{n+1}d_K^n=\beta_1^n\alpha^n-\beta_2^n\alpha^n-d_I^{n-1}h^n-h^{n+1}d_K^n=0$. (Stacks prints the correction as $(d\circ h^n+h^{n+1})\circ d$; it is $d\circ h^n+h^{n+1}\circ d$.)

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy, line 6481), direct argument of the proof (lines 6498-6537)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 4, $\psi=\varphi q$ for a morphism of complexes $\varphi:M^\bullet\to I^\bullet$. Since $M^\bullet$ is acyclic (step 5) and $I^\bullet$ is bounded below with injective terms, [lem-weil-pbc-acyclic-map-to-injective-nullhomotopy] gives $t^n:M^n\to I^{n-1}$ with $\varphi^n=d_I^{n-1}t^n+t^{n+1}d_M^n$. As $q$ commutes with the differentials, $\psi^n=\varphi^nq^n=d_I^{n-1}(t^nq^n)+(t^{n+1}q^{n+1})d_L^n$. Hence $\beta_1^n-\beta_2^n=d_I^{n-1}k^n+k^{n+1}d_L^n$ with $k^n=\bar h^n+t^nq^n:L^n\to I^{n-1}$, i.e. $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are homotopic; by step 3 this proves the lemma for the original $L^\bullet$.
